contexts.text: By the aura, or breath of the day () is signified the time when the Church had something of perception left. AC 220. AC 221.
Like a... pure and very gentle aura. HH 413:2.

The second and third posterities of the Most Ancient Church... live in an aura of light, so to speak, of resplendent pearl, and sometimes in a diamond one; for in the other life there are wonderful auras, of innumerable variety. SE 4081.
a. Affections and thoughts (from marriage love) are represented by diamond auras sparkling as with carbuncles and rubies, and this with deliciousnesses which affect the interiors of the mind.
This mist was an aura of phantasy with which they were inspired.
A bright cloud veiled them over, in which there was an aura of wisdom, by means of which their sanity came back.
The Angels cannot open their mouths to utter the word gods, for the heavenly aura in which they live is antagonistic to it.
(The highest atmosphere, called the aura.) See Atmosphere.

In Heaven no one can utter [the phrase], a Trinity of Persons, each of whom is by himself God, for the very heavenly aura itself, in which their thoughts fly and undulate, as sound does in our air, is antagonistic to it.

When I was departing, they represented to me an aura composed of chariots and horses, as they appeared, small and very numerous, just as if there were actually such an aura of beautiful horses and chariots; together with a tinge of sky-blue; saying, that they so treat their guests when they are going away.
